title: A thermodynamic design theory of self-replicators, confirmed by a predicted non-biological replicator

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a theory that predicts a chemically driven self-replicator before it is built. Starting from a specified fuel, surrounding bath conditions and library of possible reactions, the theory would identify a particular replicating structure, predict its growth and energy dissipation, and specify conditions under which it could transmit variations that selection amplifies. The confirming experiment would construct the predicted non-biological system and test those predictions prospectively. This is a proposed capability, not an achievement established by the supplied evidence.

Thermodynamic constraints provide a starting point: the supplied review reports that Jeremy L. England's Statistical Physics of Self-Replication derives a lower bound on heat production involving replication dynamics, internal entropy and durability under specified assumptions. A design theory would have to go substantially further than such a constraint. It would need to connect allowable energy flows to actual chemical structures, reaction pathways and copying behavior, drawing on chemical kinetics and evolutionary chemistry as well as nonequilibrium thermodynamics.

significance.text: Conditional significance: successful prospective design would give chemical replication and heredity a quantitative physical design basis. The immediate advance would be a non-biological replicator whose structure, growth, dissipation and heritable behavior were predicted before construction. That would turn thermodynamic reasoning into a demonstrated method for designing a system with selectable heredity, rather than only explaining constraints on a system already known.

England's analysis motivates investigating physical constraints on replication and natural selection, but its scope does not justify an unrestricted assertion that every hereditary system must dissipate free energy in the same way. The reviewed derivation concerns specified driven nonequilibrium processes; its discussion identifies conditions including diffusive, microscopically reversible dynamics and a time-symmetric drive. Any proposed design theory must state which assumptions apply to its chemical system and where its predictions cease to hold.

Conditional downstream possibilities include better experiments on plausible routes to chemical heredity, components for synthetic cells and systems capable of sustained evolutionary change. None follows automatically from designing one replicator. An origin-of-life explanation would additionally require historically plausible chemistry and environments; synthetic cells require integrated functions beyond copying; and open-ended evolution requires more than the amplification of a few predefined variants. Predicting how quickly selection acts would also require kinetic and population-level information. Feasibility and timelines remain uncertain.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central open target is a prospective mapping from specified chemical driving and reaction chemistry to a particular replicating structure, its growth and its dissipation. The supplied evidence establishes a thermodynamic foundation for asking this question, but does not establish whether this full capability remains absent across the field as of November 1, 2026. A bound on physically allowed behavior is not itself a method for choosing molecules or predicting which structure will form.

Scientific and engineering synthesis: a useful theory must reconcile energetic feasibility with reaction kinetics and molecular specificity. It must identify pathways that produce additional copies, account for competing reactions and degradation, and predict whether the proposed structure can persist under the selected drive. Predicting a permitted heat budget alone cannot determine a doubling time or establish that copying will occur. Selectable heredity adds another requirement: variants must retain distinguishable properties through repeated replication, and those properties must affect their relative propagation under defined conditions.

Measurement is part of the challenge. Heat per doubling depends on the accounting boundary: fuel consumption, background reactions, maintenance and degradation can contribute to the observed energy balance. The experimental interpretation must distinguish replication from aggregation, externally imposed copying or an increase in material that does not transmit identity. These are proposed design and measurement requirements, rather than barriers independently quantified by the supplied sources.

current_state.text: The supplied review identifies a complete retained HTML rendering of England's Statistical Physics of Self-Replication, internally identified as arXiv:1209.1179. It contains the abstract, derivation, applications and references, with no reported extraction truncation. According to that review, the paper derives a lower bound on heat production involving growth rate, internal entropy and durability under stated assumptions. This supports the existence of a thermodynamic constraint; it does not establish prospective prediction of a new replicator's structure and selectable heredity.

The historical dating requires qualification. The research associates England's work with Journal of Chemical Physics 139, 121923 (2013), while the reviewed HTML rendering displays August 9, 2026. The supplied review does not independently verify the journal citation or explain the displayed date. The full retained rendering provides more evidence than the candidate's abstract-only account suggests, but it does not establish what the earlier researcher actually read; no inspected journal PDF is documented.

The supplied bibliographic account identifies a Kolchinsky paper as Journal of Chemical Physics 161, 124101, dated September 23, 2024, DOI 10.1063/5.0213466. The research attributes to it a challenge to a universal interpretation connecting dissipation with growth and decay. However, the source index contains no retained text for this paper, so that conclusion, its precise scope and the publication details cannot be verified from document content here. The earlier statement that an interpretation was withdrawn is therefore not established: a reported later challenge would not by itself demonstrate a retraction or concession.

The supplied bibliographic account also identifies a Kolchinsky paper as Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B 380, 20240436, dated October 2, 2025, DOI 10.1098/rstb.2024.0436. The research describes a bound relating affinity, replication rate and fitness for autocatalytic replicators, illustrated using published thermodynamic data. No retained source text is available, so the detailed result and empirical illustration remain unverified here. If accurately described, an illustration using existing data would still be distinct from prospective design and construction of a new replicator.

The supplied materials contain no retained evidence establishing a preregistered de novo replicator meeting the proposed target. Their bounded freshness-search record is empty, so they also cannot establish the field's complete status as of November 1, 2026. Missing source captures limit assessment of the later papers; they are not evidence that those papers' reported results are false.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed first demonstration: before construction, preregister the molecules, reaction library, fuel or other drive, bath conditions, predicted replicating structure, expected doubling time and expected heat per doubling. State the theory's assumptions, measurement boundaries, uncertainties and conditions under which the prediction is expected to fail. The prediction should be specific enough to distinguish the intended replicator from alternative products and to prevent retrospective selection of a successful structure.
completion_criteria.label: Preregister specific replicator predictions with uncertainties and failure conditions

completion_criteria.text: Then demonstrate autonomous replication sustained by the specified drive, with measured growth and heat per doubling within a factor of two of the preregistered predictions. The factor-of-two tolerance is a proposed benchmark, not an established thermodynamic standard. Controls without the drive should establish its role in sustaining replication; the protocol should account for any transient behavior supported by residual fuel or stored free energy.
completion_criteria.label: Replication growth and heat match predictions within factor-of-two tolerance

completion_criteria.text: Define replication, heredity and selection tests in advance. Show that the system produces additional copies rather than merely aggregating or accumulating reaction products, and that copying is not imposed externally. Demonstrate that distinguishable variations persist through repeated replication and that selection amplifies them under specified conditions. The replicator must not be an evolved biological polymer whose sequence was copied from life; that exclusion is a proposed boundary for this innovation, not a conclusion of the cited thermodynamic analysis.
completion_criteria.label: Non-biological autonomous copying transmits variations amplified by selection

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and generality tests: repeat the experiment across independent preparations and obtain independent laboratory reproduction with transparent protocols and uncertainty estimates. A successful first system would establish prospective design within its tested conditions. A broader design theory would require additional predictions across distinct structures, reaction libraries or driving conditions, including documented failures and applicability limits. Finite tests can establish demonstrated breadth, not literal universality.
completion_criteria.label: Independent laboratory reproduction with transparent protocols and documented applicability limits

related_concepts.text: Roster-based comparison: THR-12, Predictive thermodynamic design of far-from-equilibrium chemical reaction networks, is the closest overlap. Both seek to predict chemical behavior from driving conditions and reaction chemistry. THR-09 adds the specific requirements of self-replication and selectable heredity; THR-12 includes non-replicating chemical functions. A general network-design method could support THR-09, but a successful non-replicating network would not satisfy this entry's target.

Roster-based comparison: THR-11, Operational temperature and entropy for far-from-equilibrium matter, concerns how thermodynamic quantities are defined and measured away from equilibrium. Such methods could help specify THR-09's energy and entropy accounting, but would not by themselves predict a copying structure. THR-01, A computable thermodynamic potential for far-from-equilibrium continuum transport, similarly shares the ambition of making nonequilibrium thermodynamics predictive, while addressing continuum transport rather than molecular replication and heredity.

Roster-based comparison: THR-07, Synthetic chemomechanical engines whose efficiency approaches biological molecular motors, shares the challenge of converting chemical driving into organized molecular behavior. Its defining output is mechanical work and conversion efficiency; THR-09's is additional copies with selectable hereditary variation. THR-03, General-purpose digital computation near the Landauer scale, provides a related energy-and-information theme, but thermodynamic limits on computation do not supply a theory of chemical copying, molecular structure or evolutionary dynamics.

unresolved_issues: The complete field status as of November 1, 2026 remains undetermined because the supplied freshness-search record is empty.
The 2024 and 2025 Kolchinsky papers lack retained source text; their precise conclusions, assumptions, publication details and reported empirical illustrations remain unverified here.
The relationship between England's claimed 2013 journal citation and the HTML rendering's displayed August 9, 2026 date remains unexplained.
The supplied evidence does not establish a withdrawal, retraction or author concession concerning a universal interpretation of the earlier replication bound.
The prospective design capability's feasibility, development timeline and achievable breadth remain unknown.

Operational definitions of copying, inherited variation, selection, heat accounting and prediction uncertainty would need specification for a concrete experimental proposal; the factor-of-two benchmark has no established-standard status.

brief.title: Designing chemicals that copy themselves
possible: Researchers could choose a chemical fuel and surrounding conditions, then predict a structure that copies itself before building it. They could calculate how fast it would multiply, how much heat it would release, and when inherited differences would help some copies spread.
why: This would give researchers a quantitative basis for designing chemical copying and heredity—the passing of traits between copies. It could help them investigate how chemical heredity begins and develop components for artificial cells.

sources.showed: England derived a lower limit on heat production during self-copying under specified physical assumptions. The limit depends on growth, durability and changes in the copying system's internal state.
sources.cited_for: Physical laws can constrain the heat produced during copying.
sources.not_established: The calculation does not predict a new chemical structure that copies itself and passes on variations.

sources.showed: This theoretical paper challenges a universal interpretation linking energy dissipation—the release of usable energy—with growth and decay.
sources.cited_for: The relationship between energy dissipation, growth and decay requires limits on where it applies.
sources.not_established: A challenge to a universal interpretation does not establish a method for designing a chemical copying system.

sources.showed: This theoretical paper describes a bound linking chemical driving strength, copying rate and reproductive success in systems that promote their own copying, illustrated with published data.
sources.cited_for: Physical constraints can connect chemical driving with copying and selection, where some inherited variants spread more successfully.
sources.not_established: An illustration using existing data does not demonstrate prediction and construction of a new copying system.

shown: Jeremy L. England derived a minimum heat output for self-copying under specified physical assumptions. His work provides a physical constraint on replication. Predicting a particular new chemical structure and demonstrating its inherited variations remains a separate goal.
missing: The theory must connect specified fuel, conditions and possible reactions to a particular copying structure, its growth and its heat output.
An experiment must build the predicted system and distinguish genuine copying from clumping or the accumulation of reaction products.
The system must pass distinguishable variations through repeated copying, with some variants spreading more successfully.
Independent laboratories must reproduce the result, and further predictions must establish how broadly the theory applies.

milestones.label: Specific predictions registered before construction
milestones.explanation: A public advance prediction would specify molecules, reactions, fuel, surroundings, copying structure, growth and heat, with assumptions, uncertainties and failure conditions. This would make success distinguishable from a retrospective fit.

milestones.label: Copying speed and heat match predictions
milestones.explanation: Autonomous copying would have to match predicted growth and heat per doubling within a factor of two, with controls accounting for residual fuel. This would test whether the specified drive sustains copying as predicted.

milestones.label: Independent chemical copying passes on selectable variations
milestones.explanation: Predefined tests would have to show autonomous copying, persistent inherited differences and their amplification by selection, without copying a biological sequence from life. This would establish non-biological copying with selectable heredity.

milestones.label: Independent laboratories reproduce the result and establish limits
milestones.explanation: Independent preparations and laboratories would have to reproduce results using transparent protocols and uncertainty estimates. Further predictions across different systems would establish the theory's breadth and limits.

uncertain: It remains unknown whether such a design theory is feasible and how widely it could apply.
Copying, inherited variation and heat accounting need precise definitions for a decisive experiment.
The factor-of-two tolerance is a proposed benchmark, rather than an established scientific standard.

page.title: Thermodynamic design of synthetic self-replicators
page.definition: A thermodynamic and kinetic theory identifies a synthetic chemical self-replicator—a system that catalyses making copies of itself—from specified fuel, surroundings and reaction chemistry before construction. Experiments confirm its predicted structure, growth, heat release and transmission of variations amplified by selection.

goal.need: For steady-state flow reactors satisfying Kolchinsky’s 2025 model assumptions, excluding a competitor with 1% lower fitness requires replication affinity of at least 4.61RT per mole, calculated from σ ≥ −ln s. Affinity measures chemical driving free energy; R is the gas constant and T temperature. This constrains selection without identifying a replicating molecule. A design theory would connect such energetic constraints to molecular identity and measured copying behavior.

completion.title: A new synthetic replicator confirms prospective predictions of structure, growth, heat and selectable heredity.
completion.criterion: From specified fuel, bath conditions and available reaction chemistry, a theory identifies one synthetic chemical replicator before construction. The constructed system confirms its predicted molecular structure, replication rate, heat released per replication, transmission of distinguishable variants and their selective amplification. Quantitative observations agree with the prospective predictions under explicitly stated experimental uncertainties and acceptance criteria. Replication uses synthetic chemistry rather than biological replication machinery.
completion.set_by: Atlas fallback; no outside body’s composite prospective-design test was identified.
completion.basis: Searches covered the supplied thermodynamic papers, the National Research Council report, Otto’s research programme, the synthetic-life roadmap, and programme, standard, prize and protocol criteria. No composite prospective-design test was found. England’s heat bound and Kolchinsky’s affinity bound constrain replication; neither selects molecular structures. The fallback requires one experimentally confirmed prediction, without imposing an unsupported numerical tolerance.

milestones.title: A synthetic chemical system catalyses the formation of copies of itself.
milestones.criterion: The system autonomously catalyses production of additional copies from precursors, meeting Otto’s functional definition of self-replication. Reported result: Morrow, Colomer and Fletcher demonstrated seed-accelerated formation of a synthetic micelle-forming surfactant on 1 March 2019. Their high-concentration seeded comparisons used three reactions per condition.
milestones.set_by: Community convention: functional definition of self-replication stated by Otto in An Approach to the De Novo Synthesis of Life, characteristic (i).
milestones.threshold_quote: autonomously catalyze the formation of copies of itself

milestones.title: Chemical fuel maintains a synthetic replicator while its molecules undergo formation and destruction.
milestones.criterion: Continuous fuel consumption maintains a replicator population away from equilibrium despite molecular turnover; stopping fuel allows the population to decay toward equilibrium. Morrow and colleagues demonstrated this in synthetic surfactant micelles on 1 March 2019. The steady-state and decreasing-fuel experiments each used three reactions; the increasing-fuel experiment used two. This establishes fuel-dependent persistence, without measuring heat per replication.
milestones.set_by: Community convention of dissipative self-replication, operationalized by Morrow, Colomer and Fletcher in A chemically fuelled self-replicator, Figure 5; their experimental test concerns micelles.
milestones.threshold_quote: This work establishes the conditions required for metastable replicators to persist by the continuous consumption of chemical energy.

milestones.title: Synthetic replicators transmit mutations whose effects on reproduction produce natural selection.
milestones.criterion: Copying produces changes in the information-bearing molecular structure that pass to subsequent generations and affect a functional property. Competition for resources favors variants through that property. These are the roadmap’s mutation, inheritance and selection criteria, without its additional requirement of open-ended evolution. Liu and colleagues reported selection for precursor-producing photocatalytic activity in two synthetic replicator systems in October 2025.
milestones.set_by: Community convention articulated by the synthetic-life roadmap workshop in Kriebisch and colleagues, A roadmap toward the synthesis of life, discussion of the overarching goal.
milestones.threshold_quote: the fitter mutants will thrive at the expense of others—the principle of natural selection.

milestones.title: A new synthetic replicator confirms prospective predictions of its structure, growth and heat release.
milestones.criterion: Before construction, a theory identifies a replicating molecular structure from specified fuel, surroundings and available reaction chemistry, and quantitatively predicts its replication rate and heat released per replication. Construction confirms the structure and quantitative predictions under stated experimental uncertainties and acceptance criteria. The energy accounting distinguishes heat release from Gibbs free-energy dissipation. This intermediate result leaves prospective prediction of selectable heredity for completion; the cited thermodynamic bounds do not report it.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback: searches of thermodynamic replication papers, synthetic-life roadmaps, programmes, standards, prizes and protocols found no published prospective structure–growth–heat validation threshold.

not_found: No published experiment was found that prospectively predicts and confirms molecular identity, growth, heat release and selectable heredity together.
The full 2025 Liu paper could not be opened at the publisher or repository; the opened university abstract establishes two systems but supplies no experimental replicate counts.

results.finding: For an existing self-replicating RNA, the estimated heat bound is 7 kcal/mol; no new experiments.
results.detail: The paper derives a heat bound using an existing replicator’s reported growth and durability. It does not prospectively identify and construct a new structure or predict and confirm its growth rate and heat release.
results.quote: Here, we undertake to make this intuition rigorous and quantitative by deriving a lower bound for the amount of heat that is produced during a process of self-replication in a system coupled to a thermal bath.

results.finding: Fuel-maintained synthetic vesicles: sample size not stated; no surfactant detected 12 hours after fuel flow stopped.
results.detail: Continuous hydrogen peroxide supply sustained vesicles while surfactant formed and broke down; stopping the supply led to decay toward equilibrium. A catalyst promoted surfactant breakdown.
results.quote:

results.finding: Synthetic fiber replicators: five repeats showed a fueled steady state with hexamers comprising 60–70% of building blocks.
results.detail: Formation and destruction occurred during fueling, and the hexamer share declined after oxidant addition stopped. Reductant addition continued initially, and the authors could not firmly establish the relative thermodynamic stabilities of the replicators; decay of the replicator population toward equilibrium was not demonstrated.

results.finding: Synthetic surfactant micelles accelerated their own formation; seeded and control conditions used three reactions each with 15 mM seed.
results.detail: Seeded reactions produced new surfactant faster than controls under both octanethiol conditions.
results.quote: In this way the aggregates act as catalysts for their own formation and self-replicate.

results.finding: Fuel maintained replicating surfactant despite turnover; three reactions per condition included a reduction to 5 μL h⁻¹.
results.detail: Continuous oxidant supply regenerated a precursor and sustained the population. After fuel supply stopped, the surfactant was consumed and the system decayed toward equilibrium.
results.quote: Once fuel supply is halted, the entire system degrades towards equilibrium.

results.finding: One synthetic vesicle-forming system showed seed-accelerated surfactant formation; sample size not stated.
results.detail: Surfactant 7 formed from thiol 6 and disulfide 2. Seeding eliminated the lag period, consistent with autocatalytic formation.

results.detail: Seeding accelerated trimer production from interconverting macrocycles. The authors describe assembly and fiber breakage as enabling exponential growth.

results.finding: In five repeats, fueled competition favored hexamer replicators, which accounted for 60–70% of building blocks after 16 hours.
results.detail: The competing ring sizes differed in replication and destruction rates, but the study does not demonstrate mutations transmitted through copying. The hexamer's greater model-reaction catalytic activity was not shown to cause its selection.

results.finding: In two synthetic self-replicator systems, selection favored mutants better able to catalyse production of their own precursors.
results.detail: Selection depended on photocatalytic activity, a functional trait of the replicator mutants.
results.quote: Here we show the emergence of Darwinian evolution in two systems of self-replicating molecules in which natural selection favours replicator mutants best capable of catalysing the production of the precursors required for their own replication.

results.finding: Two synthetic self-replicating molecular systems showed selection for catalytic function; reaction sample size was not reported.
results.detail: The source describes self-replicating molecules whose mutants catalyse production of precursors required for their own replication.
